answer:
HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded, NLSY79; N=7,522 complete cases): Considering academic characteristics (ASVAB cognitive ability) substantially weakens—and for race, largely explains away—the apparent effects of Socioeconomic Status and race on educational attainment (our proxy for BA-degree completion). Direction and magnitude:

(1) SES. The total SES effect on educational attainment is strong (1979 grade: +0.51 grade-levels per SD of SES; ever-college-dorm attendance: OR≈3.2). Once academic ability is included, the SES effect roughly HALVES (grade: +0.23, p<.001; dorm: OR≈1.9)—an attenuation of ~46–55% that is robust across every specification tested (college-dorm outcome 46%, binary race 49.5%, MICE m=20 50.2%, Sample-ID strata 53.7%; single SES components 30–67%). Formal bootstrap causal mediation shows ~54% of the SES effect (95% CI 45–61%) is INDIRECT, operating through academic ability, with a statistically significant residual DIRECT SES effect. There is also a significant SES×ability interaction (−0.19, p<.001): the SES advantage is larger among low-ability respondents. Net: academic characteristics account for about HALF of the SES gradient; the other half is a direct SES effect.

(2) Race — Black. The modest Black disadvantage in attainment (grade −0.11, p=.03; college-dorm OR 0.71, p=.002) is essentially ELIMINATED once academic ability is controlled (grade +0.06, ns; dorm OR 0.98, ns; strata −0.055, ns). Mediation shows the Black gap is carried almost entirely by a significant NEGATIVE indirect path through lower ASVAB (indirect −0.17, 95% CI −0.21 to −0.13), while the direct racial effect is small and non-significant. Thus academic characteristics explain essentially all of the observed Black attainment gap.

(3) Race — Hispanic. A SUPPRESSION pattern: naively there is no net gap, but holding ability constant reveals a significant POSITIVE direct effect (grade +0.42; dorm OR 3.6) that is cancelled by a NEGATIVE indirect path through lower average ASVAB (−0.35). The net Hispanic effect is ~0 only because lower academic ability offsets a positive direct effect.

LIMITATIONS (stated plainly). The dataset contains NO direct BA-degree variable; we therefore estimate "educational attainment / college attendance," NOT strict BA-degree conferral (proxies = 1979 highest-grade-completed [continuous/ordinal] and ever-in-college-dorm 1981–1996 [binary]). The 1979 grade predates the 1981 ASVAB, so the mediation is an explanatory association, not a strict causal chain. The Black/Hispanic "attenuation" is a suppression, not a clean mediation, so a single mediation-proportion is not meaningful for race. Missingness (ASVAB ~12%, income ~20%, parents' education 6–14%) is handled by complete cases (N=7,522) with MICE (m=20) sensitivity; results are directionally consistent.

payload.hypothesis: Academic characteristics (ASVAB ability) mediate roughly half of the SES effect on educational attainment (BA-completion proxy): the SES gradient halves (~50% attenuation; ~54% of the effect indirect, 95% CI 45–61%) once ability is controlled, with a significant residual direct SES effect and a significant SES×ability interaction. Academic ability also accounts for essentially the entire Black attainment gap (which disappears after controlling ability, via a significant negative indirect path), while the Hispanic effect is a suppression (a positive direct effect masked by lower average ability). The race 'attenuation' is a suppression, not a clean mediation.
payload.workflow: 1) Audited data/nls_raw.csv (N=12,686, 61 cols): confirmed NO direct BA-degree variable; ASVAB 'Z-score' columns are raw ASVAB scores (mean~475) and were re-standardized. 2) Variables: outcome = highest-grade-completed 1979 (primary, continuous) + ever-in-college-dorm 1981-1996 (cross-validation, binary); SES = standardized mean of log family net income 1979 and max(parent education) [wealth 1985/1990/1996 as sensitivity]; race = 3-category (Black/Hispanic/non-Black-non-Hispanic ref); academic characteristics = mean of 4 standardized ASVAB sections. 3) Model A (SES + race dummies + controls: sex, age1979, family size) vs Model B (+ ASVAB) on complete cases N=7522, heteroskedasticity-robust SE (HC1 OLS / HC0 logit); reported coef/SE/p and attenuation ratio for SES and each race dummy. 4) Bootstrap (2000) causal mediation: total/direct/indirect + mediation proportion with 95% CIs (each X holding the other race groups + SES + demographics constant). 5) Interaction terms SES*ASVAB, Black*ASVAB, Hispanic*ASVAB. 6) Robustness: college-dorm outcome (logit), binary race, single-component SES (income/parent-ed/wealth/full), MICE m=20 (OLS chained equations, Rubin pooling), and Sample-ID (20 strata) fixed effects. Executed script: master_analysis.py (Parts 1-6, runs end-to-end ~1.5 min); outputs: combined_results.txt.
